stem:
Priya finds a bar magnet at home. It breaks into two pieces when it falls on the floor. She thinks she can now get one piece with only a North pole and one piece with only a South pole.
Which statement about the broken magnet is correct?

options.text: Each broken piece is a complete magnet with both a North pole and a South pole.
One broken piece has only a North pole and the other has only a South pole.
Both broken pieces lose their magnetism and have no poles.
The bigger piece keeps both poles and the smaller piece has no poles.

teacher.key_rationale: Breaking a magnet always produces smaller magnets, each with a North and a South pole; a single isolated pole cannot be obtained. Option B is the trap of assuming the pole at the broken end remains alone.
